segments.text: Header of the kernel `asmread`, the hand-written load-only loop. The whole-chip test times this function in part L, in part C and in control I [Ref9]. Part A times `asmread` in other binaries, bw_old and bw_new [Ref16].
segments.heading: Kernel `asmread`: the hand-written load-only loop, function `k_asmread`

segments.text:
Start address `4ac0` (hexadecimal) and name of the function. **The loop is lines 66 to 76.**
- Address range: `4ad4` to `4afc`. That is 11 instructions, 44 bytes of code. Loop start modulo 64: 20.
- Bytes read per loop pass: 256 B.
- Load instructions per loop pass: 8 (`ldp`, 32 B each).
- Other instructions per loop pass: 3 (`add`, `cmp`, `b.cc`).
- The loaded values are not used.
- Source: the asm text of the macro `DEF_ASMREAD` in bwx12.c, used as `DEF_ASMREAD(asmread, 0)` [Ref4].

These 5 instructions run once per call, before the loop. The compiler wrote them.
- `stp d8, d9, [sp, #-64]!` lowers the stack pointer by 64 B and stores `d8` and `d9` there. Lines 63 to 65 store `d10` to `d15` in the same 64 B.
- Reason: the loop overwrites `q8` to `q15`. The calling convention AAPCS64 requires that `d8` to `d15` hold their old values when a function returns [Ref4].
- `add x1, x0, x1, lsl #3` (line 62) computes the end address `x1 = x0 + 8 * n`. Source: `end = a + n`.

The loop starts at line 66 (the label `1:` of the source). The 8 `ldp` instructions read the 256 B that start at `x0` into `q0` to `q15`, 32 B per instruction. No instruction uses the loaded values. These are the 8 loads of `k_read` (lines 4 to 11) with other register numbers.
- Lines 66 to 76 are the 11 instructions of the asm text of the source, in the same order. The compiler chose only the registers: `x0` for the pointer and `x1` for the end address.
- The comment in bandwidth.c says that the compiler cannot add arithmetic, reorder or drop anything inside such an asm block [Ref3].
Moves the pointer forward by 256 B (`0x100` = 256). Source: `add %[p], %[p], #256`.

`cmp x0, x1` compares the pointer with the end address. `b.cc 4ad4` jumps back to line 66 while the pointer is lower (unsigned compare). The source writes `b.lo`, another name of `b.cc`. `k_read` tests the same condition with swapped operands (`cmp x1, x0`, then `b.hi`).
These 4 instructions run once per call, after the loop. They load `d8` to `d15` back from the stack. `ldp d8, d9, [sp], #64` also raises the stack pointer by 64 B.
`ret` returns to the caller. The function returns no value.
